atoms.1: The symptoms and physical findings suggest involvement of the lower motor neurons (tongue fasciculations).
atoms.2: The symptoms and physical findings suggest involvement of the upper motor neurons (pronounced jaw jerk reflex).
atoms.3: The combination of dysphagia, slurred speech, tongue fasciculations, and a pronounced jaw jerk reflex is highly indicative of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
atoms.4: The clinical presentation is consistent with ALS, which affects both upper and lower motor neurons.
atoms.5: The most likely diagnosis is amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
atoms.6: Baclofen is typically used for spasticity, not specifically for improving survival in ALS.
atoms.7: Dextromethorphan and quinidine are used for treating pseudobulbar affect in ALS, not directly improving survival.
atoms.8: Edaravone has been shown to slow the decline in functional status in ALS.
atoms.9: Riluzole is the only drug known to modestly prolong survival in ALS by approximately 2-3 months.
atoms.10: Tizanidine is used for muscle spasticity, not specific for improving survival in ALS.
atoms.11: Among the given options, Riluzole is the drug most likely to improve survival in a patient with ALS.
